title: A stretchable, electroconductive tissue adhesive for the treatment of neural injury

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1 (Synthesis and chemical characterization), ELP sequence description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the pentapeptide repeats were "modified every five units of isoleucine with valine (([VPGVG]₄[IPGVG])₁₄)" and then "The substitution of isoleucine with valine ... provides tunability" and "strategically substituting valine for isoleucine". The stated sequence shows VPGVG units in which the valine of every fifth repeat is replaced by isoleucine (IPGVG), i.e., the substitution direction is the opposite of what is written, and the two sentences also contradict each other ('substituting isoleucine with valine' vs. 'substituting valine for isoleucine').

DM = (integrated area of methacrylate protons)/(integrated area of reference peak × number of protons in methacrylate group) is not a valid normalization: the reference (Trp aromatic) integral is not divided by its own proton number, so the ratio is not a per-residue molar ratio, and the expression yields a dimensionless ratio that is reported as a percentage (18%, 33%) without a ×100 factor or a defined denominator of modifiable residues.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (NMR characterization) and Section 3.1 — use of tryptophan as NMR reference
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: "an aromatic peak at 7.5 ppm related to Trp (W) residue was used as a reference" for DM quantification, but the custom ELP is described as ([VPGVG]₄[IPGVG])₁₄ plus a Lys-Cys-Thr-Ser tail — this sequence contains no tryptophan, so the stated internal reference does not exist in the described macromolecule.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods (cyclic tensile test) vs Figure 2 caption (g, h)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Methods state the cyclic tensile test was run for "10 cycles", whereas the Figure 2 caption reports "representative cyclic tensile stress–strain curve for 3 cycles" and "energy loss ... after 8th tensile cyclic measurements". The number of cycles reported in the figure does not match the described protocol and the two caption panels are mutually inconsistent.

The statistics section states "error bars were evaluated as the mean ± standard deviation (SD)", but the Figure 2 caption states "error bars indicate the standard error of the means". SD and SEM are different quantities; the reported dispersion measure is contradictory.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, ¹H NMR assignment of Bio-IL (Figure 1d discussion)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: "the appearance of a sharp peak at δ ~ 3.1 ppm corresponds to the three hydrogen atoms of the ammonium ion" — choline's quaternary ammonium bears three methyl groups, i.e., nine equivalent protons (N(CH₃)₃), not three hydrogens; the quaternary nitrogen itself carries no protons. The integration/assignment is chemically incorrect.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, assignment of disulfide formation in crosslinked hydrogel NMR (Figure 2c, region 2)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same spectral window is assigned to two different species: multiplets at "1–1.3 ppm (C−H bonds of −CH₂ groups)" from acrylate–methacrylate reaction and "multiplet peaks between 1.0 and 1.1 ppm confirmed the formation of the disulfide (−S−S−) bonds". Cysteine β-CH₂ protons adjacent to a disulfide resonate near 2.9–3.3 ppm, not 1.0–1.1 ppm, so the disulfide assignment is implausible and conflicts with the neighboring assignment.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1 / Methods — solution ¹H NMR of the photocrosslinked hydrogel
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: NMR is described as solution-state ¹H NMR in DMSO-d6, yet the authors report spectra of the "crosslinked mELP/Bio-IL hydrogel" and derive a degree of crosslinking (Eq. 2) from peak areas before and after crosslinking. A covalently crosslinked, insoluble network cannot be dissolved for quantitative solution NMR; no solid-state/HR-MAS or gel-swelling protocol is described, so the quantification method as described cannot work.

"A total of two rats were used in the study: one was euthanized on day 7 and the other on day 28. For each group, four samples were tested." With one animal per time point there is no biological replication; all four 'replicates' per group are pseudo-replicates from a single animal, and these same 8 implants are said to serve both histology (explanted with surrounding tissue) and mass-loss degradation (explanted without tissue), which cannot both be done on the same samples. Statistical comparisons based on this design are not supportable.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract (final sentence) and Translational Impact Statement
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims the hydrogel "effectively enable[s] sutureless surgical sealing of neural injuries and promote[s] tissue regeneration" and that it aids "in the transmission of neuro signals to support normal nerve function". No in vivo nerve injury/repair model, no regeneration outcome, and no neural electrophysiology were performed; the only in vivo work is subcutaneous implantation, and the only conduction test is ex vivo muscle twitch in rectus abdominis tissue. The conclusions overstate the reported evidence.

"electric pulses of 50 ms were applied ... from a voltage source (potentiostat; Agilent, 4284A)". The Agilent/HP 4284A is a precision LCR meter, not a potentiostat or pulse voltage source; the stated instrument cannot deliver the described 50 ms stimulation pulses, so the stimulation setup is misdescribed.

The Methods describe only one methacrylation condition ("15% (v/v) methacrylic anhydride ... added dropwise"), whereas the Results state that two polymers were made, "with a high degree of methacrylation (DM) using 15% (v/v) MA and with a lower DM using 7.5% (v/v) MA". The second synthesis condition is absent from the Methods.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1 — methacrylate proton chemical shift ranges
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The methacrylate/methacrylamide proton peaks of mELP are first reported "in the region of 5.5 to 6.3 ppm", but when discussing crosslinking the same peaks are stated to be "at 5.34–5.68 ppm, which were related to the methacrylate group of mELP". The two stated ranges for the same protons do not match.

"few bioadhesive materials based on fibrin (e.g., Evicel®, TISSEEL™) and cyanoacrylate (e.g., Dermabond™) have been commercially available for clinical treatments of nerve injuries". Dermabond (2-octyl cyanoacrylate) is a topical skin adhesive approved for external skin closure, not a product indicated/marketed for nerve injury repair; the attribution of clinical nerve-repair use to this product is incorrect.

The abstract states "the engineered hydrogel supported in vitro viability and proliferation of human glial cells", but the described assay used transwell inserts with the hydrogel physically separated from cells seeded on tissue-culture plastic. This indirect (leachate) test demonstrates absence of cytotoxicity, not that the hydrogel 'supports' cell adhesion/proliferation on or in the material.
